    <item>
      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Delaware hit by rare November tornado</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado</link>
      <description><p>Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina</p><p>The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.</p><p>Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe</p><p>After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands.       <description><p>With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea</p><p>At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.</p><p>Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/ng-interactive/2026/aug/02/this-is-where-democracy-beats-totalitarianism-ukraines-drone-strike-force-takes-the-fight-to-russia">the work had become almost mundane:</a> they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/how-ukraine-struck-kerch-bridge-symbol-vladimir-putin-rule">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/kessler-twins-assisted-dying-decision</link>
      <description><p>Pop-singing sisters, who died aged 89 last year, described their declining health and desire to depart life together</p><p>Alice and Ellen Kessler, the identical pop-singing twins who chose to jointly end their lives through assisted dying last year, said they had “reached rock bottom” due to health problems and had been relieved to be able to die together.</p><p>The German sisters, who became huge television stars in the 1960s and 70s, especially in Italy and the US, said a catalogue of health conditions had left them with no desire to carry on living.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/kessler-twins-assisted-dying-decision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘They were keeping it for a rainy day’: Ukraine’s Kerch bridge attack is proof Kyiv still has cards to play</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-kerch-bridge-attack-russia-crimea-analysis</link>
      <description><p>Partial demolition of bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea is obvious embarrassment to Putin days before meeting with Xi and Trump</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/17/europe-ukraine-russia-crimea-kerch-bridge-attack-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Ukraine’s attack on the Kerch road bridge overnight is the culmination of weeks, and perhaps months, of military operations plus years of industrial development, during which Kyiv has developed its own cruise missiles and long-range drones.</p><p>The demolition is not quite total, because the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-strikes-critical-damage-russia-kerch-bridge-crimea">rail bridge is still standing</a>, one line in operation – but the attack is an obvious embarrassment to Russia two days before Vladimir <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/xi-jinping-donald-trump-vladimir-putin-world-peace-trilateral-says-china">Putin is due to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping</a> in Shenzhen.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ukraine-kerch-bridge-attack-russia-crimea-analysis">Continue reading...</a></description>

French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action.

Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:21:47 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>EU economics chief warns France and Belgium must reduce deficit and public debt</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-eu-economics-chief-warns-france-and-belgium-must-reduce-deficit-and-public-debt</link><description>
France and Belgium must bring down their public debt and deficit levels, European Union economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis warned on Tuesday as he unveiled the European Commission's autumn economic forecast. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">065f0570-e281-11f1-84fb-2734eec1674a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:00:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'A message to drug gangs': life sentences for 'barbaric' Marseille murders</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-a-message-to-drug-gangs-life-sentences-for-barbaric-marseille-murders</link><description>
Two leading figures in Marseille's drug-trafficking underworld were sentenced to life imprisonment on Monday for a triple murder in 2020. Anti-drugs activist Amine Kessaci, whose brother was among the victims, hailed the verdict as a "message to the narcocracy".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1288fd3c-e282-11f1-91a0-f16e280f34ca</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:59:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg">AFP - THIBAUD MORITZ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French presidential candidates clash over tax, housing and the minimum wage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-french-presidential-candidates-clash-over-tax-housing-and-the-minimum-wage</link><description>
Five candidates for the 2027 French presidential election on Monday evening wrangled over issues including the cost of living crisis, the minimum wage and single parents in a live televised debate. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/46a83610-e259-11f1-aa75-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T194753Z-1720879303-RC27POAQ40KA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/46a83610-e259-11f1-aa75-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T194753Z-1720879303-RC27POAQ40KA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">20e86fa6-e26a-11f1-8eb4-bd86e9020d76</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:50:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/46a83610-e259-11f1-aa75-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-16T194753Z-1720879303-RC27POAQ40KA-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS.jpg">via REUTERS - KENZO TRIBOUILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Le Pen to end France’s financial aid to Ukraine if elected president</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-le-pen-to-end-france-s-financial-aid-to-ukraine-if-elected-president</link><description>
Marine Le Pen on Monday said that France would provide no further financial aid to Ukraine if she is elected president next year, after a meeting with Kyiv's ambassador in Paris.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b7bf9cb2-e254-11f1-8bb3-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T110825Z-1468534110-RC23VHA3GD6L-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-LEPEN-PENSIONS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b7bf9cb2-e254-11f1-8bb3-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T110825Z-1468534110-RC23VHA3GD6L-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-LEPEN-PENSIONS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2a8883b2-e278-11f1-aabb-77a008c9523d</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:50:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b7bf9cb2-e254-11f1-8bb3-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-13T110825Z-1468534110-RC23VHA3GD6L-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-LEPEN-PENSIONS.jpg">© Gonzalo Fuentes / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for second nationwide strike over demands for higher wages</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-france-braces-for-second-nationwide-strike-over-demands-for-higher-wages</link><description>
France is braced for its second nationwide strike in less than a fortnight on Tuesday, after unions called on nearly six million public-sector workers to take to the streets to demand higher wages.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">678bf058-e266-11f1-92d6-39b0dbf095fa</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/470371ba-e05b-11f1-9950-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-14T153531Z-25633910-RC2PNOAZ102X-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French actor Depardieu withdraws appeal against conviction for sexual assault</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-actor-depardieu-withdraws-appeal-against-conviction-for-sexual-assault</link><description>
French actor Gérard Depardieu has apologised after withdrawing his appeal against a May 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">514af00c-e1a1-11f1-82bc-0f0371ba9765</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:19:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French cybercrime unit probes massive cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-cybercrime-unit-probes-massive-cyberattack-on-la-poste-subsidiary</link><description>
A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f7093a68-e114-11f1-aa3b-e18acb043b04</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:01:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg">REUTERS - ERIC GAILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Harki families take legal action over children's 'ghost graves' in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-harki-families-take-legal-action-over-children-s-ghost-graves-in-france</link><description>
Five families of Harkis – Algerians who fought for the French during Algeria's war of independence – have filed a legal complaint seeking answers over children who died in the 1960s in a former Harki camp in the south of France, and whose remains have since disappeared.

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim</link>
      <description><p>International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits</p><p>Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.</p><p>A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/apr/17/deutsche-bank-faces-action-over-20bn-russian-money-laundering-scheme">been caught being used to launder billions of dollars</a> for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/17/uk-jobs-market-wage-growth-payrolls-unemployment-milburn-china-us-chips-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/nvidia-jensen-huang-statement"><strong>Jensen Huang says he would be ‘honored’ to return to Nvidia as CEO</strong></a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/16/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-china"><strong>Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia CEO becomes a political proxy war</strong></a></p></li></ul><p><strong>China has threatened to retaliate against the US after Washington tightened restrictions on remote access to AI chips and servers.</strong></p><p>At a press conference on Tuesday, China’s foreign ministry spokesperson <strong>Guo</strong> <strong>Jiakun</strong> said Beijing would take “necessary measures” to safeguard its own interests, saying:</p><p>“The US has repeatedly overstretched the concept of national security, abused export controls and even interfered in China’s normal trade and technological cooperation with other countries, unjustifiably suppressing the development of China’s high-tech industries.”</p><p>“This is the worst situation possible for China because the last thing they want to see is any new restrictions on their access to chips.”</p><p>“Export controls are what upset them practically more than anything else right now other than maybe Taiwan.”</p><p>Deutsche plotted an expansion of its <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/bf775dda-4148-49f9-a8b4-a4a02f44207e">notorious Russia business</a> under chief executive Christian Sewing, over-ruling the fears of its compliance team about the bank’s Kremlin-connected clientele as geopolitical storm clouds gathered.</p><p>The bank <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/784cbdc7-c852-4081-b1e5-390779e9fad1">accidentally leaked Trump’s tax statements</a> during his first presidential term and kept the mistake secret from the White House, with Sewing briefed on its handling of the crisis.</p><p>Deutsche processed almost $600mn of suspicious <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/72ac6fee-55f3-4db5-a1e3-873ef39c0b96">payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein</a>, a far higher figure than previously known.</p><p>A <a href="https://www.ft.com/content/4f8dae68-bfec-43bd-bef6-b830815ec538">catalogue</a> of compliance deficiencies, governance weaknesses, ineptitude and technology failings, including a confession to regulators that Deutsche was in effect “operating outside of law and order”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/17/uk-jobs-market-wage-growth-payrolls-unemployment-milburn-china-us-chips-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/17/wales-v-portugal-nations-league-football-live-score-updates</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Nations League updates from the 7.45pm GMT kick-off</p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live">Live scores</a> | <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/jurgen-klopp-germany-project-football-daily-newsletter">Today’s Football Daily</a> | And <a href="mailto:Scott.Murray@theguardian.com">email Scott</a></p></li></ul><p><strong>Craig Bellamy speaks to S4C.</strong> “[Portugal] can score four or five as well [as Denmark] …on the day they were quite unlucky … the opportunities they created … they didn’t convert them … we’re aware of their threat … at times they will be open as well … even when we’re suffering, there’s always an opportunity to exploit the space … no doubt we can impose our game … now we want the results … tonight that’s the aim … can we make them suffer? … it’s a tough test … but an exciting one as well.”</p><p><strong>Portugal make four changes after that 4-1 defeat at home to Denmark.</strong> Rúben Dias is suspended so António Silva comes into the defence. João Neves, João Cancelo and Francisco Trincão step up; João Félix, Alberto Costa and Rúben Neves sit down. The Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs is also on the bench, sporting Portugal’s fancy new post-Cristiano continental-style No 7.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/17/wales-v-portugal-nations-league-football-live-score-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>French FA chief officially begins bid for Fifa presidency</p></li><li><p>Uefa’s choice hints at ‘support from other continents’</p></li></ul><p>Philippe Diallo, Europe’s candidate to fight Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency, said he had received “strong signs of support from other continents” as he launched his campaign in Paris on Tuesday.</p><p>The French Football Federation president also said he had contacted Kozo Tashima, who announced his candidacy this month, and would try to convince him to “join forces”.       <title>Wayne Rooney says he contemplated taking own life during playing career</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wayne-rooney-contemplated-taking-own-life-during-playing-career-mental-health</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Former England footballer opens up on mental health</p></li><li><p>‘It was probably the lowest point’ at Manchester United</p></li></ul><p>Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai.</p><p>He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the <a href="https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/wayne-rooney-growing-up-in-the-spotlight-fatherhood/id1527545442?i=1000802417716">Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan</a> podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wayne-rooney-contemplated-taking-own-life-during-playing-career-mental-health">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable | Ewan Murray</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland</link>
      <description><p>The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job</p><p>The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.</p><p>There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/switzerland-scotland-nations-league-match-report">4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland</a> was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/jurgen-klopp-germany-project-football-daily-newsletter</link>
      <description><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2022/nov/14/football-daily-email-sign-up"><strong>Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!</strong></a></p><p>Barely six weeks ago, Jürgen Klopp’s big home debut in the Germany dugout ended in a deeply frustrating <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/27/nations-league-germany-greece-serbia-netherlands-norway-portugal">1-0 Nations League defeat to Greece</a> – but the manager tasked with returning <em>Die Mannschaft</em> to relevance claimed not to care. “I’m completely unbothered,” Klopp trilled unconvincingly. “I’ve lost far more matches than I would have liked, but as long as you draw the right conclusions, a loss is ultimately a piece of information – no different from a win.” It was a quote straight out of the Pierre Sage playbook for unfussed continental coaches – and probably worried a few German FA suits, given Klopp had already threatened to quit <em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/24/germany-confirm-jurgen-klopp-new-head-coach">at his own unveiling</a></em> over potential media intrusion and criticism. “If you say tomorrow, ‘he’s [sh!t]’, tell me to my face and I’m out,” Klopp roared to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/24/germany-confirm-jurgen-klopp-new-head-coach">trembling hacks in July</a>. That imagined confrontation now looks unlikely to take place, because his Germany side are suddenly very good indeed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/jurgen-klopp-germany-project-football-daily-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Head coach excited by ‘high potential’ of players</p></li><li><p>Striker Goodwin and keeper Cox in squad for first time</p></li></ul><p>Sarina Wiegman says the potential in England’s emerging young players helped convince her to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/19/sarina-wiegman-signs-contract-extension-england-women-euro-2029">extend her contract</a> until the end of 2029’s European Championship.</p><p>The Lionesses head coach, whose previous deal was due to expire next year, gave first senior call-ups to the striker Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox on Tuesday as she named her squad for December’s two-leg World Cup qualifying playoff against Ukraine.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sarina-wiegman-england-young-talent-contract-isobel-goodwin-squad">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes</link>
      <description><p>A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation</p><p>“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.</p><p>The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/diego-maradona-argentina-world-cup">Argentina’s football folklore</a> are spliced with excellent archive material.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France </p><p>There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.</p><p>Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/04/slavia-prague-arsenal-champions-league-match-report">at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days</a>, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/14/arsenal-everton-premier-league-match-report">Premier League’s youngest goalscorer</a>. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter</link>
      <description><p>In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations</p><p>I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group.</p><p>As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/janine-van-wyck-south-africa-wafcon-book-extract-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience</p><p>Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.”</p><p>Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/26/harry-kane-ends-englands-25-year-wait-for-a-mens-ballon-dor">last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London</a> for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/he-wants-to-change-lives-the-story-behind-bukayo-sakas-socrates-award">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Sloppy Socceroos given a reality check as Jordan dominate in friendly win</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/australia-jordan-scocceroos-international-friendly</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Jordan 2-0 Australia (Al-Taamari 34, Ali Olwan 90+3)</p></li><li><p>Socceroos had just one effort on target in defeat</p></li></ul><p>In their final game of 2026, the Socceroos were given a reminder that they remain a work in progress, beaten 2-0 by Jordan in an international friendly where the scoreline failed to reflect the first-half siege the victors laid on their opponent’s goal, nor the unforced errors and brain fades that helped doom the Australians’ hopes of firing a shot in response.</p><p>Optimism was high for those in green and gold after their comfortable <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/mcgree-helps-socceroos-put-drama-behind-them-and-leave-qatar-reeling">win against the reigning Asian champions Qatar</a> on Friday but very quickly on Tuesday it was made apparent that the Jordanians were to provide far more spirited opposition. This time around it would be the Australians that were to be the subject of a first-half onslaught, as a Jordan team inspired by Musa al-Taamari launched forward with wicked pace and ruthless intent whenever the opportunity, or space left by the Socceroo defence, presented itself.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/australia-jordan-scocceroos-international-friendly">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/fifa-accused-climate-record-failure-aramco-deal-tournament-expansion</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Groups question ‘sincerity’ to meet emissions pledges</p></li><li><p>Oil giant is a major sponsor of football governing body</p></li></ul><p>The United Nations has been asked to review Fifa’s status as a signatory to a key environmental initiative, with complainants arguing football’s governing body has a “record of failure” on climate action.</p><p>Fifa <a href="https://inside.fifa.com/sustainability/news/fifa-joins-the-un-sports-for-climate-action-framework">is a signatory</a> to the UN’s Sports for Climate Action Framework, a coalition which seeks to persuade sporting organisations to “work together to achieve a climate-resilient future”. Under the framework, signatories agree to cut their greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 and to “partner with key stakeholders to deliver joint climate action”. They can have their status as a signatory removed, however, if “sincerity in participation or ability to participate is a cause for concern”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/fifa-accused-climate-record-failure-aramco-deal-tournament-expansion">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Ebullient journalist, magazine editor and broadcaster whose passion for music and football shone through all his work</p><p>Danny Kelly, who has died aged 69, influenced music journalism and sports broadcasting for more than four decades. Humour, enthusiasm and encyclopedic knowledge were the hallmarks of his work as a writer and editor at the New Musical Express (NME) and Q magazine, and throughout his online, TV and audio career, most prominently around his passion for football.</p><p>In 1997 Kelly helped set up Football 365, one of the earliest football websites, and still one of the most popular in the UK. He hosted radio shows on BBC 5 Live, TalkSport, BT Sport and Times Radio, as well as many podcasts including The View from the Lane, about the team he had supported since childhood, Tottenham Hotspur.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/nov/17/danny-kelly-obituary">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish</link>
      <description><p>Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead</p><p>Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/feb/11/tottenhams-soaring-dreams-for-thomas-frank-quickly-hit-the-buffers-of-grim-reality">after being sacked by Tottenham in February</a>, but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”.</p><p>Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-pierre-sage-sacked-steve-parish">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor</link>
      <description><p>Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw</p><p>Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. <strong>Suzanne Wrack</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/chelsea-manchester-city-womens-super-league-match-report">Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Pochettino: I’d tell Guardiola to ‘take it’ if he’s offered US coaching job</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/mauricio-pochettino-pep-guardiola-usmnt-manchester-united</link>
      <description><p>As he prepares to depart for Manchester United, the outgoing US coach held court on a number of topics, including what he’d change about soccer in America</p><p>Outgoing US head coach Mauricio Pochettino and former Manchester City head coach Pep Guardiola have a long, storied past. The two faced each other as players, when Guardiola was at Barcelona and Pochettino was making his name across town at Espanyol. They faced each other 22 times as managers in the Premier League and the two share a mutual respect – and intensity – when it comes to their approach to playing and coaching alike.</p><p>So when Guardiola visited Yankee Stadium in September to serve as New York City FC’s pre-match hype man before their rivalry match with Red Bull New York, Pochettino – in town anyways to scout the match – made it a point to sit with him during the game. He brought along his assistant coach and confidant Jesús Pérez, and US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/mauricio-pochettino-pep-guardiola-usmnt-manchester-united">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title><![CDATA[France 24 - Infos, news & actualités - L'information internationale en direct]]></title><description>France 24 décrypte l’actualité internationale, politique, l’économie, l’environnement, la culture, le sport, en France et à l’international avec analyses, des interviews, des reportages exclusifs, des magazines et des documentaires.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:51:37 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Journal de l'Afrique</category><title>Francophonie : face à l'impasse, l'élection du secrétaire général repoussée d'un an</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/journal-de-l-afrique/20261117-francophonie-face-%C3%A0-l-impasse-l-%C3%A9lection-du-secr%C3%A9taire-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ral-repouss%C3%A9e-d-un-an</link><description>
L'élection du secrétaire général de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), au coeur d'un bras de fer entre République démocratique du Congo et Rwanda, a été reportée d'un an lundi faute de consensus, un "compromis" diversement accueilli. La sortante rwandaise Louise Mushikiwabo, qui a dénoncé des "pressions nombreuses et fortes" à son encontre, restera en place jusqu'à la tenue du nouveau scrutin, auquel le Rwanda ne présentera pas de candidat.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1393afbe-e206-11f1-aa0f-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/DN198070-A-01-20261111.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1393afbe-e206-11f1-aa0f-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/DN198070-A-01-20261111.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">353de444-e2b6-11f1-8853-031b5c15add3</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:51:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Célia CARACENA</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>CAN 2027: l'Algérie s'écroule au Togo, la Tunisie ne gagne toujours pas</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261117-can-2027-l-alg%C3%A9rie-s-%C3%A9croule-au-togo-la-tunisie-ne-gagne-toujours-pas</link><description>
L'Algérie avait besoin d'une victoire pour espérer une qualification dès la 4e journée de ces éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. À la place, les Fennecs se sont complètement écroulés au Togo (3-0). La Tunisie, qui avait besoin de gagner pour se relancer et prendre confiance, a fait match nul contre la Libye, sur fond de polémique pour un penalty sifflé trop généreusement.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a790610-e2b2-11f1-bae3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2304695297.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a790610-e2b2-11f1-bae3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2304695297.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4f90fd94-e2b2-11f1-8ad8-57dac076eb8b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:24:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6a790610-e2b2-11f1-bae3-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2304695297.jpg">NurPhoto via Getty Images - NurPhoto</source><dc:creator>Yohann Le Coz</dc:creator></item><item><title>CAN 2027: la Sierra Leone retarde la qualification de la RD Congo, la Côte d'Ivoire freinée par la Gambie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261117-can-2027-la-rdc-retarde-sa-qualification-la-c%C3%B4te-d-ivoire-ralentie-en-gambie</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">fc71cbac-e2b1-11f1-9202-bf2fcc3a9b4f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:11:37 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>CAN 2027 : la RD Congo retarde sa qualification, la Côte d'Ivoire ralentie en Gambie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261117-can-2027-la-rdc-retarde-sa-qualification-la-c%C3%B4te-d-ivoire-ralentie-en-gambie</link><description>
La Côte d'Ivoire et la RD Congo avaient besoin d'une victoire ce mardi 17 novembre, respectivement contre la Gambie et la Sierra Leone, pour valider leur billet pour la CAN 2027. Le travail n'a pas été fait. Les Léopards ont concédé le nul en toute fin de match (1-1). Les Éléphants, eux, se sont fait surprendre par les Gambiens après avoir mené au score (2-2) et voient le suspense relancé dans leur groupe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d06fdf96-e2af-11f1-b843-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B4X276N.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d06fdf96-e2af-11f1-b843-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B4X276N.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33dff87e-e2a9-11f1-868d-4937d01672fb</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 18:08:16 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d06fdf96-e2af-11f1-b843-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/000-B4X276N.jpg">© Nicolas Tucat, AFP</source><dc:creator>Yohann Le Coz</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Comment une fausse citation de Christine Lagarde a été amplifiée par un réseau de désinformation srilankais</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261117-comment-fausse-citation-christine-lagarde-amplifi%C3%A9e-par-r%C3%A9seau-d%C3%A9sinformation-sri-lanka</link><description>
Selon plusieurs publications Facebook, Christine Lagarde aurait déclaré que "les personnes âgées vivent trop longtemps", ce qui représenterait un "risque" pour l’économie. Une fausse citation attribuée à tort à la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, actuellement relayée par un réseau de désinformation basé au Sri Lanka.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ee6d5e26-e2a8-11f1-b668-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/image2-154.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ee6d5e26-e2a8-11f1-b668-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/image2-154.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1995705c-e2a9-11f1-ae40-7f6b8fd6a643</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:31:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ee6d5e26-e2a8-11f1-b668-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/image2-154.png">© X</source><dc:creator>Les Observateurs</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Record du monde : Nataliia Zharkova plonge en apnée à 124 mètres  de profondeur</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261117-record-du-monde-nataliia-zharkova-plonge-en-apn%C3%A9e-%C3%A0-124-m%C3%A8tres-de-profondeur</link><description>
Nataliia Zharkova plonge à 124 mètres et établit le record de profondeur en apnée féminine. Dans la catégorie “poids constant” où l'Ukrainienne concourt, les plongeurs descendent et remontent sans s'aider d'une corde, tout en étant soumis à une pression intense sur leurs poumons, à des besoins en oxygène accrus et à un long parcours à la nage pour regagner la surface.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/618f17d2-e2a9-11f1-b3c8-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/miniaplong%C3%A9e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/618f17d2-e2a9-11f1-b3c8-c5c0357b2a0c/w:1024/p:16x9/miniaplong%C3%A9e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">68adfd26-e2a9-11f1-abb8-d3b6d609e074</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:14:22 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Guerre en Ukraine : une partie du pont de Crimée s’effondre après des frappes de Kiev</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261117-guerre-en-ukraine-une-partie-du-pont-de-crim%C3%A9e-s-effondre-apr%C3%A8s-des-frappes-de-kiev</link><description>
L'attaque ukrainienne sur le pont reliant la Russie à la Crimée, annexée par Moscou, a été qualifiée d'"opération sans précédent" par Volodymyr Zelensky ce mardi 17 novembre. Des bombardements menés en "réponse aux frappes russes" contre les infrastructures du pays, selon le président ukrainien.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f13b7294-e2a5-11f1-9a94-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/guerreenukraine.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/f13b7294-e2a5-11f1-9a94-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/guerreenukraine.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f90b9724-e2a5-11f1-aa5f-6128cad543e7</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:05:50 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Quelle est votre madeleine de Proust ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261117-quelle-est-votre-madeleine-de-proust</link><description>
Quel goût vous ramène instantanément en enfance ? Avec “Rue du Goût Perdu”, ces souvenirs d'enfance deviennent le point de départ d'un projet autour de la gastronomie et de la transmission. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/96941996-e2a4-11f1-bf53-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/EXTRAIT-3-VIGNETTE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/96941996-e2a4-11f1-bf53-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/EXTRAIT-3-VIGNETTE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6bbd9b16-e2a4-11f1-baf8-77821a2c056c</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 17:01:29 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Amériques</category><title>Rougeole : les États-Unis perdent leur statut de pays ayant éliminé la maladie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/am%C3%A9riques/20261117-les-%C3%A9tats-unis-perdent-leur-statut-de-pays-qui-a-%C3%A9limin%C3%A9-la-rougeole</link><description>
Les États-Unis ont perdu leur statut de pays ayant éliminé la rougeole, a annoncé, mardi, l'Organisation panaméricaine de la Santé. Alors qu'elle avait été éradiquée depuis 25 ans dans le pays, cette maladie grave et très contagieuse a signé sous Donald Trump un retour en force, sur fond de baisse des taux de vaccination.
